reading_evidence: Read all nine stanzas: prescribed bed/sleep and plate/rice without need, blindness/directions and deaf/mute royal-praise questions, monkey news versus weaverbird home knowledge, new night meaning as lover meeting rather than wine/cupbearer, rice freed from food-prison into labourer hunger/belly/hands, garden possession versus creation/child teeth, colours freed from religion and new word-meanings assembly, closing plate/bed recurrence. Checked each redefinition and actor.
reason: Attach day-long labour and weariness to the returning worker, not the speaker performing the metaphorical weaving.
open_questions: Rajgan remains provisional royal praise and asar assembly.
Garden/animals and food-prison images remain unexplained; no political characters assigned.
tradeoff: Same two lines and same bodily image; no separate actor or moral added.

prior_uncertainties.note: Retains rice/hunger distinction, monkey and weaverbird, religious colours and child teeth images. Source rajgan provisionally rendered royal praise; asar as assembly. Hindi feminine speaker is provisional; source does not grammatically specify gender.

before.label: English
before.title: From This Moment
stanzas: Pillows and sheets are spread upon the bed, whether weariness is there or not
One is simply meant to sleep.
Rice is served upon the plate
Whether hunger is there or not, one is meant to eat.
For one who has no sight
Left, right, before, behind
Are all the same
Every road a destination.
The king's praises are being sung
But what can the deaf hear?
The heart's secrets are being asked for
But what can the mute say?
The monkey tucked into this branch and that
Brings news of the realm
If you would know of home and family, of human sorrow and joy
Ask the weaverbird.
Now, from this very moment, I think I shall give night another meaning
Setting it apart from wine and the cupbearer
I shall call my meeting with my lover night.
Freeing rice from the prison of food
I shall join it to hunger
After a whole day's labour, worn and weary
I shall weave it with the belly and hands of the one who has returned.
There is no use blaming
The monkeys and weaverbirds
The garden is their playground,
As little children keep their toys for their own
If they think of the garden that way, let them,
But I am joining the garden to creation and
Reading the flowers as a little child's newly sprouting teeth.
I am freeing colours from religion
And joining them to an open grassy field,
Upon this grassy field
Gathering the ever-new meanings of words
I am making an assembly
Let the rice be served upon the plate
Let the pillows and sheets lie spread.

before.label: ଓଡ଼ିଆ
before.title: ବିକଳ ମନ
stanzas: ଘନ ଅନ୍ଧାରେ କାହିଁ ମନ ବିକଳ,
ଆଖି କେବେ ଶୁଖିଲା, କେବେ ସଜଳ,
ନିଜ ହୃଦୟର ଥଳ ପାଏ ନାହିଁ,
କଜଳର କାଳିରେ ଚିଠି ଲେଖେ ମୁହିଁ।
ତୁମେ ମୋ ଭିତରେ, ମୁଁ ତୁମ ଭିତରେ,
ଯେପରି କୃଷ୍ଣ ରାଧାମୟ, ରାଧା କୃଷ୍ଣମୟ,
କାହିଁ ପ୍ରତି କ୍ଷଣେ ଏବେ ଏହା ବୁଝାଏ,
ଆମେ ତ ପରସ୍ପରର ସାଇତା ସମ୍ପଦ,
କଜଳର କାଳିରେ ଚିଠି ଲେଖେ ମୁହିଁ।
କାନଫୁଲ ଟିକେ ବି ମନକୁ ନ ମାନେ,
ସାଜସଜ୍ଜା ଯେପରି କଣ୍ଟା ହୋଇ ଲାଗେ,
ମହମରେ ବନ୍ଧା ଗୋଟିଏ ସଳିତା,
ତୁମରି ଉଷ୍ମାରେ ତରଳିଯାଏ,
କଜଳର କାଳିରେ ଚିଠି ଲେଖେ ମୁହିଁ।
ପ୍ରତି ପାଦଶବ୍ଦରେ ଚମକିପଡ଼େ,
କେବେ ଦଉଡ଼େ, କେବେ ଫେରିପଡ଼େ,
କଳା କେଶରାଶି ମୋତେ ଭୁଲାଏ,
ତାହାର ଖେଳ ଟିକେ ବି ଭଲ ନ ଲାଗେ,
ମୋ ମୁହଁକୁ ସେ ଅସ୍ଥିର କରେ,
କଜଳର କାଳିରେ ଚିଠି ଲେଖେ ମୁହିଁ।
ଜାମସେଦପୁର

before.label: English
before.title: A Restless Heart
stanzas: Why is the heart restless in this dense dark,
Eyes sometimes dry, sometimes wet,
I cannot fathom my own heart,
With kohl for ink I write a letter.
You in me and I in you,
As Krishna is filled with Radha, Radha with Krishna,
Why do I keep explaining this now, moment by moment,
We are each other's cherished keeping,
With kohl for ink I write a letter.
My earrings please me not at all,
Adornment feels like thorns,
A wick bound up in wax,
Melting only in your warmth,
With kohl for ink I write a letter.
At every footfall I start,
Sometimes I run, sometimes turn back,
My dark tresses bewilder me,
Their playfulness gives me no delight,
They torment my face,
With kohl for ink I write a letter.
Jamshedpur

reading_evidence: Read all nine lines: wrinkles marked more by experience than years, aged youth/new collapsing building, more built structures than years, head-load of brick/stone/sand, concrete civilization weight without tremor/heartbeat, ending soulless garment. Checked Hindi possessive agreement against nouns rather than inferring worker gender.
reason: Remove unsupported male identity: source possessives/participles agree with wrinkles, youth, buildings and carried objects, not conclusively with a male worker.
tradeoff: Singular they retains one worker, including one head, without selecting another gender. No change to the final metaphor.

before.label: English
before.title: A Soulless Garment
stanzas: In his wrinkles there was less age and
More experience,
His youth had grown old,
Like a new building falling down,
He had built more buildings than his years,
Carrying bricks, stone and sand upon his head,
Bearing the weight of a concrete civilization,
With neither a tremor nor a heartbeat,
It is only a soulless garment.

reading_evidence: Read all five stanzas: vanished childhood place remaining in memory, siblings entering responsibility, breeze/water/greenery preserving colour and sweetness, protective shadows, changed people and bonds beneath the tree in a search for friends. reason: Preserve bonds left behind without explicitly making the speaker choose to abandon them.
open_questions: Source trees/its/this tree number and shadow antecedent remain loose; no additional tree identified.
tradeoff: Remained behind keeps loss and location while not assigning intention; new-friend search remains unexpanded.

before.title: ପିଲାଦିନର ଚେର
stanzas: ଦେଖ, ସମୟ କେମିତି ବିତିଗଲା
ଯେଉଁ ଜାଗାରେ ଆମ ପିଲାଦିନ ଫୁଟିଥିଲା
ଏବେ କେବଳ ସ୍ମୃତିରେ ରହିଛି।
ଯେଉଁ ଭାଇଭଉଣୀମାନେ ଦିନେ ଏଠି ଖେଳୁଥିଲେ
ଏବେ ନିଜ ପିଲାଦିନକୁ ପଛରେ ଛାଡ଼ି ଆସିଛନ୍ତି
ଦାୟିତ୍ୱକୁ ଆପଣେଇ ନେଇ।
ପବନ ଏବେ ବି ପୁରୁଣା ସ୍ମୃତି ବୋହିଆଣେ,
ପାଣିରେ ତା'ର ମିଠାପଣ ରହିଛି
ଗଛମାନଙ୍କର ସବୁଜିମା
ଦିନେ ଆମ ଜୀବନକୁ ରଙ୍ଗରେ ଭରିଦେଉଥିଲା।
ତା'ର ଛାଇ ସବୁ ଦିନେ
ଆମକୁ ଦୁଃଖରୁ ରକ୍ଷା କରୁଥିଲା।
ସମୟ ସହ ଆମେ ବି ବଦଳିଯାଇଛୁ
କିଛି ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଏହି ଗଛ ତଳେ ଛାଡ଼ି ଆସିଛୁ
ନୂଆ ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ସନ୍ଧାନରେ।
